core_struggle: A working person who wants to understand what the texts say about varna and marriage, so they can explain their view to a cousin.
mirror: You want to show your cousin what the shastras say, and you want to be sure you are right.

queries.hook: The wish to understand what the texts say about varna and marriage, and the question of what makes a person pure.
queries.diagnose: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.
queries.steady: The self is not divided by birth; the one who sees the self in all sees no difference.
queries.act: Read the verses on the self and the one who sees the self in all, and let the text speak for itself.
queries.story: A seeker and a teacher, where the teacher shows that the self is one and not divided by birth.

weeks: The one who sees the self in all
emotion: curious and looking for an answer
bridge: You want to know what the Gita says about varna and marriage, and the text itself will show you that purity is of the self, not of birth.
week_thesis: Seven days from wanting to know what the texts say about varna and marriage to seeing that the texts teach purity of the self, not of birth.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the wish to understand what the texts say about varna and marriage.
week_beats.steady: You hold that the self is not divided by birth, and that the one who sees the self in all sees no difference.
week_beats.act: You try reading the verses on the self and the one who sees the self in all, and let the text speak for itself.
week_beats.story: A seeker and a teacher, where the teacher shows that the self is one and not divided by birth.

insight: You want to know what the texts say about varna and marriage, and the Gita itself will show you that purity is of the self, not of birth.
seat: a working person who wants to understand what the texts say about caste and marriage
life_context: A working person in their late twenties or early thirties who wants to understand what the texts say about varna and marriage, so they can explain their view to a cousin.
